summary: java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException while tesselating block model / Game crashes when breaking a block
description: The game crashed as I break a full block of oak wood slabs causing me to crash. 19w38a : [^crash-2019-09-18_21.01.43-client.txt] Description: Tesselating block model java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 1, Size: 1 at java.util.ArrayList.rangeCheck(ArrayList.java:653) at java.util.ArrayList.get(ArrayList.java:429) at cxj.b(SourceFile:91) at cxe.a(SourceFile:306) at dps.a(SourceFile:134) at dps.b(SourceFile:76) at dps.a(SourceFile:47) at dpq.a(SourceFile:48) at dpd.a(SourceFile:1300) at dpa.a(SourceFile:691) at dpa.a(SourceFile:535) at daj.e(SourceFile:931) at daj.b(SourceFile:564) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition version 19w38a.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Place an oak wood slab block in your world.
4. Approach the placed oak wood slab and attempt to break it using any tool or by hand.
5. Observe that the game crashes upon breaking the oak wood slab.
Observed Behavior: The game crashes specifically when breaking a full block of oak wood slabs, resulting in an IndexOutOfBoundsException during the tessellation process of the block model. This issue was observed and reported in version 19w38a. The error message indicates that the problem occurs due to attempting to access an index that is out of bounds within an ArrayList, specifically at index 1 when the size of the list is only 1. This exception arises from the method cxj.b in SourceFile:91 and propagates through various other methods related to block rendering and game logic. The crash occurs consistently when breaking oak wood slabs but does not happen with all blocks; for instance, it does not occur with scaffolding or shulker boxes placed before updating to 19w38a. Additionally, the issue seems to be linked to the visual effect of block cracking during destruction, as blocks that break instantly do not cause a crash. The game also crashes when breaking other types of blocks like quartz and netherrack under certain conditions, such as without an efficiency-enchanted tool or while jumping in the air. This bug was eventually fixed in version 19w38b.
Expected Behavior: When breaking a full block of oak wood slabs, the game should not crash. The block should break normally without any exceptions or errors, and the player should be able to continue playing without interruption. This behavior should be consistent across different types of blocks and tools used for breaking them.
